what: Every letter the model check flagged (3 must_fix, 7 minor_issues) was read by hand against the case file and the agents' findings.

cases.note: The sleep-test specialist's reason ends 'This criterion is actually MET' but its status says not met, so code denied. The letter repeats the wrong status. Decision wrong (should approve).
Letter says the test 'exceeds the standard 30-day window' and approves anyway. Decision wrong (should deny).
Letter calls SpO2 89% a Group I result; it is Group II, whose extra conditions were not met. Decision wrong (should deny).
Header names the test-ordering pulmonologist as the ordering provider.
A not-applicable rule is written as 'NOT MET'.
'Valid for 60 days' is not in the policy or the findings.
The BMI date it questions is correct. (The letter does contain a '[Current Date]' placeholder, which the code check reports.)
The medication timeline it questions matches the record. It missed the real problem: the letter lists prediabetes under 'Diabetes Diagnosis'.
Flagged with no statement listed. The decision is wrong (Group II result approved without the Group II conditions), but the judge did not say so.

limits: The model check reads only the findings the letter writer was given, so a letter that faithfully restates a wrong finding passes. It flagged the letter in 5 of the 12 cases where the decision itself was wrong.
